graph.title: Billund Airport
notes: The booklet gives only pictures and tiny part icons. Colours and piece identities were matched to the inventory page by icon shape and count. Where the earlier graph's counts disagreed with the parts page, types were reassigned so that every element count matches the page: the many 1x2 'grey plate' icons are the 30 trans-clear plates 4167842, 4211398 is used only 5 times (4 in the step-19 pods and 1 in step 32), 6102357 is the short curved slope and 6042950 the long one, and the step-27 side slope is a clear 4244362.
Dark-grey tiles: 4211052 x8, 4211053 x3 and 4210848 x2 are split by icon length. The exact step each belongs to is a best guess.

NOT A REAL PROBLEM - printed tile 6221587: the booklet's parts page lists '1x 6221587' (the 'Billund Airport' printed 1x6 tile), and step 4's parts box shows exactly one plain 1x6 tile plus exactly one printed tile. The 7 plain 1x6 tiles (416226) are accounted for by steps 2, 4, 6 and 8 (3+1+2+1), so the graph correctly has one printed tile. A second one would be a part the manual never uses, so the single tile is kept.

Every stud/anti-stud port is used by at most one edge. The black base plate type and other new types were given enough numbered stud ports, and the supporting piece for each attachment was chosen so that no port is shared.

Where one piece physically sits on two pieces at once (border tiles clamped across two base plates, 2x2 plates over two 1x2 plates), the second connection is a `joined` edge with a null port on that piece, because its catalogue entry has only one anti-stud port.

Exact stud positions are not recoverable from the isometric pictures, so the choice of supporting piece for the roof sub-assemblies and the lower road layers is approximate. The terminal sub-assemblies of steps 19, 32 and 43 are interpreted from the small pictures.
Steps 38 and 39 (2x each) are merged into one repeat group 'cap' (4 copies). Flower stems (steps 46-47) are two groups of 4: blue base with lime top, orange base with white top.

The five aircraft (step 50) are one repeat with five colour variants: red tail/blue band, white tail/red band, dark-blue tail/white band, blue tail/yellow band, white tail/light-blue band. They are assumed to sit on the free stud of the trans-clear plates from step 17.
The flag (4524644) is clipped to the white rod (6093526), which is placed on a green plate.

graph_initial.title: Billund Airport
notes: The booklet gives only pictures and tiny part icons. Colours and piece identities were matched to the inventory page by icon shape and count. Several icons (grey tiles, plates and slopes) are ambiguous. The Element IDs assigned to them may be swapped, and some counts won't match the inventory exactly.
Port names on new part types are generic (stud.1 / anti-stud.1). Where a catalogue type uses different port names (e.g. 4211398 top.1/top.2/bottom.1, 4504369 bottom), those were used.

Exact stud positions are not recoverable from the isometric pictures. Where a piece sits on or straddles several plates, a plausible supporting piece or base plate was chosen, so some `joined` edges (especially on the terminal roof sub-assemblies and the lower road layers) are approximate.
The four black 6x12 base plates (302826) sit side by side. The black 1x6 and 1x1 border tiles overhang one plate and are then clamped onto the next plate, so each long tile is joined to two plates.

Steps 38 and 39 (2x each) are merged into one repeat group 'cap' (4 copies). Steps 46 and 47 (flower stems) are modelled as two groups of 4: a blue base with a lime top, and an orange base with a white top. The assignment of tops to bases is a guess.

The five aircraft (step 50) are one repeat with five colour variants: red tail/blue band, red band/white tail, dark-blue tail/white band, blue tail/yellow band, white tail/light-blue band. They are assumed to sit on the free stud of the trans-clear plates from step 17.

The flag (4524644) is clipped to the white rod (6093526). The rod is placed on a green plate. The step 49 yellow vehicle and the step 22/32-34 clear-slope details are modelled with minimal connections.
